requested.title: LLM relay follows unvalidated redirects and re-resolves user-controlled endpoints

parsedVerdicts.reasoning: The current runner stores the user-derived generic provider URL after `completionUrl` checks only URL syntax and the HTTP(S) scheme, then calls Node's bare `fetch(relay.url)` with its default redirect behavior. The account BYOK route does call `assertPublicHttpUrl` at registration, and `getUserByok` repeats that check before each run, but those checks only validate a DNS result at that earlier point; neither passes a pinned address to the runner. A malicious public provider can therefore pass validation and then return a 307/308 redirect from its `/chat/completions` endpoint to an internal address, which preserves the relay's POST request and is followed without any target validation. DNS rebinding also works because the runner independently resolves the hostname when `fetch` connects, after the application's validation has completed. The self-hosted Compose configurations attach both `agent-runner` and `minddy` to `private` and `agent_egress`, so the runner can reach internal service names and network addresses unavailable to external callers. The relay streams the upstream response back to the sandbox, making this more than a blind request primitive, although response usefulness depends on the target's response format. The registration probe is also a bare `fetch` and follows redirects, so it does not reliably prevent configuration of such an endpoint. `safe-fetch.ts` has the necessary redirect-by-redirect validation and pinned-request mechanism, but the standalone runner neither imports nor implements either protection. Git history shows the vulnerable relay was introduced in commit `18465f29`, with no subsequent change to this file that addresses it.
